record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Polynomial-size families with perfect state transfer
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with adjacency matrix A and transition matrix U(t)=exp(itA). Find an infinite family of graphs that admit perfect state transfer between some pair of vertices, where perfect state transfer means that U(t)e_u = γ e_v for some time t and unit complex number γ, and such that the size of each graph is bounded above by a polynomial in its diameter.

evidence.quote: Formally, perfect state transfer occurs at a G between vertices u and v at time t if there is a complex number γ of absolute value 1 so that U(t)e_u = γ e_v.
Find an infinite family of graphs for which there is perfect state transfer, and the size of the graph is bounded by a polynomial in the diameter.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{V\times V}$. For $t\in\mathbb{R}$, define the unitary transition matrix
$$U(t)=\exp(itA).$$
For vertices $u,v\in V$, we say that $G$ admits perfect state transfer from $u$ to $v$ if there exist a real time $t$ and a complex number $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|=1$ such that
$$U(t)\,e_u=\gamma\,e_v,$$
where $e_w$ denotes the standard basis vector indexed by the vertex $w$. Let $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ denote the graph diameter of $G$ and $|V(G)|$ its number of vertices.

Problem: Construct an infinite family $\{G_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ of finite connected graphs with the following two properties:
1. For each $n$, the graph $G_n$ admits perfect state transfer between some pair of vertices.
2. There exists a polynomial $p$ such that $|V(G_n)|\le p(\mathrm{diam}(G_n))$ for every $n$, and $\mathrm{diam}(G_n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

Equivalently, exhibit perfect state transfer at arbitrarily large distances in graphs whose vertex count grows only polynomially with the distance.
artifact.category_tag: Continuous-time quantum walks / perfect state transfer
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, originally posed by Godsil, remains open. Known infinite families exhibiting perfect state transfer (e.g., variants of paths, cycles, Cartesian powers of small graphs, diamond chains, and certain circulants) either have bounded diameter or have size growing super-polynomially in the diameter. Recent work has obtained polynomial-size families for the weaker notion of "peak" state transfer, but not for perfect state transfer.

status_evidence.title: Selected open problems in continuous-time quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: Find an infinite family of graphs for which there is perfect state transfer, and the size of the graph is bounded by a polynomial in the diameter.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Peak state transfer in continuous quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: A family of graphs achieving peak state transfer at arbitrarily long distances with size bounded polynomially in the distance.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-size families are known for peak state transfer (a weaker notion), suggesting perfect state transfer version is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Perfect state transfer is poly-time
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses time complexity of perfect state transfer; does not resolve the polynomial-size-in-diameter problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related results address time, not graph size versus diameter.
